question: Should OpenClaw adopt this 15-surface localization coverage manifest and fail-closed CI gate as the permanent repository-wide release-governance contract, including the shared locale registry’s cross-surface scope?
rationale: This decides product policy and ongoing ownership—not a mechanical defect—because the manifest controls what localization maturity means and when repository automation blocks promotion.

options.title: Sponsor a bounded governance contract
options.body: Approve a documented v1 scope, named owning areas, and compatibility expectations, then require the branch to rebase and provide exact-head proof before normal review continues.

options.title: Keep localization checks surface-local
options.body: Decline the repository-wide manifest and retain existing UI, CLI, native, and docs validation under their own owners without a shared release gate.

options.title: Defer the release gate
options.body: Accept contributor guidance and inventory exploration later, but postpone any required CI or promotion-blocking behavior until a maintainer RFC is accepted.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a bounded governance contract
recommendation.body: Approve a documented v1 scope, named owning areas, and compatibility expectations, then require the branch to rebase and provide exact-head proof before normal review continues.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the proposed series and can clarify its intended boundaries, although final product acceptance requires a repository maintainer.
